correctness.rationale: Independence is exact: xi=mean(epsilon_i) is jointly Gaussian and orthogonal to each column noise difference, so r0=a-R1/(m+1)+xi. Conditioning on R_{-j}, Gaussian regression gives the residual orthogonal column u_j in t=d-m+1 dimensions with nonsingular isotropic Gaussian density, whose inverse radius has finite p moment exactly when p<t by polar integration. The independent xi makes conditional alpha_j normal with variance sigma^2/((m+1)||u_j||^2), giving the matching divergence lower bound even when its mean shifts. For sufficiency, finite Gaussian moments and the u_j inverse bound control alpha. Since Z=H alpha+B, H has full column rank and B=y0-Proj_col(R)r0 has moments of all orders, no tail cancellation is possible. Tikhonov pseudoinverse operator norm <=1/(2sqrt(lambda)), giving all polynomial moments. New independent checks reconstructed Gaussian inverse covariance matrices and least-squares/output decompositions; these tests cannot prove the rare-event integrability.
residual_risks: Requires fixed affinely independent input points, strictly positive iid isotropic Gaussian variance, exact arithmetic. Not an adaptive iterated Anderson convergence theorem.
Infinite-moment boundary follows from Gaussian small-ball integral, not finite sampling.
